description: The greenhouse effect is not primarily a problem: it is the invisible mantle that prevents the Earth from freezing. The real issue is when you thicken it too quickly.

hero.hook: Without the greenhouse effect, the Earth would be an icy desert. With too much, it overheats.

blocks.text: Imagine a car closed in the sun: the windows let the light in, but the heat has difficulty getting out. The passenger compartment heats up. The  of Earth works a bit like that, with air instead of glass. [[Greenhouse gases (GHG)]]

This phenomenon is **natural** and vital. Without it, the average temperature of the globe would fall towards **-18 °C**. With him, we are around **+15 °C**. The current problem is not its existence: it is its rapid **amplification** by our activities.

The Sun mainly sends visible light. The atmosphere lets it pass. The land and oceans heat up, then radiate this energy back in the form of **infrared heat**, waves that are “longer” than visible light.

blocks.caption: Industrial emissions reinforce the greenhouse effect.

blocks.text: Certain gases, , absorb this heat and radiate it in all directions, including towards the ground. Nitrogen and oxygen, the majority in the air, hardly do this job. Water vapor, **CO₂** and **methane** do this very well. [[Greenhouse gases (GHG)]]
The name “greenhouse effect” is a bit misleading. A real greenhouse heats mainly by blocking the rising hot air. The atmosphere traps heat by absorbing infrared rays.

sections.title: How the planet keeps its heat

blocks.text: Since the industrial revolution, coal, oil and gas have been burned. This carbon, buried underground for millions of years, returns to the air. Deforestation also reduces forests that absorbed CO₂. Raising and growing rice adds methane, about **80 times** more “heating” than CO₂ over 20 years.

Result: the CO₂ concentration increased from approximately **280** to more than **420** parts per million. Such a level had not been seen since , around **Z3** million years ago, when seas were higher. [[Pliocene]]
The , which synthesizes the work of thousands of climatologists, is clear: the warming since 1950 is unprecedented over millennia, and its human origin is established. [[IPCC]]

More energy in the air and oceans means more extremes: drier droughts, more violent rains, melting glaciers and ice caps, rising sea levels. And an accelerator: when the white ice disappears, the dark soil and water absorb more sunlight. The  is falling, and the planet is warming even faster. [[Terrestrial albedo]]
Venus shows the “packed” greenhouse effect: an atmosphere of 96% CO₂, and about **460 °C** on the ground, enough to melt lead.

sections.title: What a more energetic climate changes

blocks.text: The international objective aims to remain below **+1.5°C** or **+2°C** compared to the pre-industrial era, to avoid dangerous thresholds such as the thawing of , which would release even more methane. [[permafrost]]
Two levers: **reduce** emissions (clean energy, sobriety, forests) and **adapted** to what is already committed. CO₂ remains in the air for centuries: what we emit today lasts a long time.
Without a natural greenhouse effect, the Earth would freeze around **-18 °C**. Its amplification by fossil fuels pushes CO₂ to levels not seen for **3 million years**.
